subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: If y = a cos(sin x) + b sin(sin x), prove that y₂ + (tan x)y₁ + y cos²x = 0.

mark_split.label: Differentiate once by the chain rule

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what the chain rule gives you and why the tan x term is in the result.

steps.label: Differentiate once by the chain rule
steps.margin_note: First mark. The inner function is sin x, so every differentiation of the outer part brings out a factor cos x. Naming the bracket P keeps the second differentiation short.
lines: y = a cos(sin x) + b sin(sin x)
The inner function is sin x, whose derivative is cos x, so
y₁ = [−a sin(sin x) + b cos(sin x)]·cos x
Write P = b cos(sin x) − a sin(sin x),   so   y₁ = P cos x

recall.must_convey: That the chain rule gives y₁ = [b cos(sin x) − a sin(sin x)] cos x.
accept: use the chain rule with sin x as the inner function
y one is the bracket times cos x
differentiating the inside gives a cos x factor
chain rule vaadali, lopala sin x undi kabatti cos x vasthundi
call the bracket P so that y one is P cos x

steps.why: Both terms have sin x inside, so both bring out the same factor cos x. Taking it outside once keeps the next differentiation to two terms instead of four.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the cos x factor from the inner function.
Writing cos(sin x) as cos x sin x.
steps.memory_tip: Differentiate outside first, then multiply by the derivative of what is inside.

steps.label: Differentiate a second time
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Differentiating P returns −y cos x, because P and y swap places under differentiation. That single fact is what makes this question short.
lines: P′ = [−b sin(sin x) − a cos(sin x)]·cos x = −y cos x

recall.must_convey: That P′ = −y cos x, so y₂ = −y cos²x − P sin x.
accept: differentiating P gives minus y cos x
use the product rule on P times cos x
y two is minus y cos squared x minus P sin x
P differentiate cheste minus y cos x vasthundi
P and y change into each other when differentiated

steps.why: P is built from the same two functions as y with the roles exchanged, so its derivative returns y. That is why the answer closes with only y, y₁ and y₂ in it.
common_mistakes: Differentiating P cos x as P′cos x only, leaving out the second product term.
Writing P′ as +y cos x and losing the sign of the whole result.
steps.memory_tip: y differentiates into P and P differentiates into −y — the same pattern as sin and cos.

steps.label: Form the middle term
steps.margin_note: Third mark. This one line explains why the identity carries a tan x: it converts y₁, which has a cos x, into the P sin x that y₂ needs cancelling.
lines: (tan x)y₁ = (sin x / cos x)·P cos x

recall.must_convey: That (tan x)y₁ = P sin x, because the cos x cancels against the cos x in tan x.
accept: tan x times y one is P sin x
the cos x cancels with the cos x in tan x
tan x is sin x over cos x so only sin x is left
cos x cancel ayipoyi P sin x migulutundi
that is why the identity has a tan x in it

steps.why: y₂ contains −P sin x, and nothing else in the identity can remove it. Multiplying y₁ by tan x produces exactly +P sin x, so the tan x is there to cancel that term.
common_mistakes: Writing (tan x)y₁ as P sin x cos x, forgetting the cancellation.
Using cot x in place of tan x, which leaves a cos²x/sin x factor.
steps.memory_tip: tan x = sin x / cos x, so multiplying anything that carries a cos x by tan x trades that cos x for a sin x.

steps.label: Add the three terms
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Two cancelling pairs: P sin x against −P sin x, and y cos²x against −y cos²x. Write both pairs down before claiming the result.
lines: y₂ + (tan x)y₁ + y cos²x = (−y cos²x − P sin x) + P sin x + y cos²x
The two P sin x terms cancel, and so do the two y cos²x terms

recall.must_convey: That the P sin x terms and the y cos²x terms cancel in pairs, giving 0.
accept: add all three and everything cancels in pairs
P sin x cancels and y cos squared x cancels
the sum is zero so it is proved
anni cancel ayi zero vasthundi
the two pairs cancel and nothing is left

steps.why: The identity is exactly the statement that these two pairs cancel. Showing both pairs is the proof; a bare "= 0" is not.
common_mistakes: Writing the answer as 0 without showing which terms cancelled.
Substituting P back and expanding, which makes the cancelling much harder to see.
steps.memory_tip: Two terms in, two terms out: each of the three parts of the identity is there to kill one term of y₂.
